title: Recency-aware length-bucketed sampler for per-tenant calibration packs
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Define and implement a reproducible sampling strategy to generate per-tenant (per-domain) calibration packs for FP8/INT8 quantization validation. The sampler must preserve production distribution properties relevant to inference quality while keeping pack sizes bounded for repeatable calibration runs. Key constraints: (1) production prompt traffic is heavy-tailed across intents and tenants, (2) KV-cache and sequence length distributions affect quantization error, (3) datasets must be de-duped and privacy-safe, and (4) we need deterministic seeds and manifest metadata for later auditing.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler produces one calibration pack per tenant with configurable size (default 10k prompts) and deterministic manifest including sample timestamp, original request id (hashed), intent cluster, token-length bucket, and recency-weight value.
Per-tenant packs match production token-length distribution within ±5% per bucket (buckets: 0-32,33-128,129-512,512+).

Calibration runs using the generated packs produce INT8/FP8 accuracy delta vs FP16 baseline within thresholds defined in the quantization playbook (see links): <1.0% top-level metric regression for high-volume tenants; <2.5% for long-tail tenants under controlled review.
Sampling pipeline supports deduplication (exact-response and fuzzy embedding-based duplicates) and logs counts of removed items in the manifest.
Sampling code is unit-tested and produces identical manifests given fixed RNG seed; integration test runs reproducibly in CI with sample fixture data.
Documentation published with sampling knobs, recommended defaults, and migration steps for existing calibration packs.
updates: 2026-02-10: Ticket created. Drafted high-level sampler design and constraints. Linked to quantization playbook and runtime kernel notes.

2026-02-16: Design review with PM. PM requested per-customer weighting option so enterprise tenants with contractual SLAs can be oversampled. Action: add 'tenant_weight' field in manifest and sampling config (Mateo).

2026-02-22: Engineering spike completed. Implemented prototype that reads anonymized production log export, computes token-length histogram per tenant, and performs exponential recency weighting (half-life configurable). Found skew in some tenants dominated by API health-check prompts; added filtering by agent_id and low-entropy heuristics.

2026-02-28: Data-privacy review: hashing scheme for request_id approved (HMAC-SHA256 with rotation). Added config flag to drop full-text artifacts for privacy-sensitive tenants; manifest will include embedding vectors only when allowed.

2026-03-03: Integration tests added for deduplication step using embedding similarity threshold 0.85 (cosine). Observed ~12% duplicate rate in sample tenant A; adjusted default duplicate threshold to 0.9 for long-tail tenants to keep diversity.

2026-03-07: Submitted PR #4421 with core sampler implementation and manifest schema. Requesting code review from runtime and infra owners. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4421

2026-03-09: PM feedback: include 'intent_quota' controls so product teams can guarantee minimum representation for critical intents. Added 'intent_quota' to sampling config; updated acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12: First end-to-end run on staging for three tenants completed. Uploaded evaluation artifacts and dashboard. Metrics: token-length bucket match within target for 2/3 tenants; one tenant requires special handling due to synthetic traffic. Next: tweak health-check filters and run a second pass.
acceptance_test_plan: Run sampler on anonymized 7-day production export for 3 tenants and verify manifest checksum matches expected for seed=42.
Run calibration on INT8/FP8 variants using generated packs and compare core metrics (exact-match on canned intents, embedding-similarity on open intents, token-logprob delta) against FP16 baseline.
Validate dedup counts and ensure privacy flags correctly remove raw text when config set.
Perform SLA-focused run for one enterprise tenant using tenant_weight=3 and confirm representation quotas are satisfied.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive dedup reduces calibration pack size and speeds runs but can under-represent repetitive, high-frequency prompts that may be important to production latency behavior. Default dedup threshold chosen to balance diversity and practicality.
Decision: use exponential recency weighting with configurable half-life (default 30 days). This preserves recent drift while allowing historical examples for rare intents.
Follow-up: consider a two-stage sampler for next quarter that first ensures intent quota and then fills remaining slots with recency-weighted draws to maintain both coverage and freshness.
Observed blocker: staging export contains synthetic 'health-check' traffic that inflates short sequences. Add a filter by user_agent and by low-entropy token distributions to exclude these.
